articles.title: Maria do Carmo (PL) promete reforçar efetivo policial no Amazonas | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidata do PL ao governo do Amazonas participou de caminhada no bairro Manoa, em Manaus, neste sábado (29), onde apresentou propostas para a segurança pública.
articles.summary: Maria do Carmo (PL) propõe valorização salarial de policiais e convocação de concursados para reforçar a segurança pública no Amazonas durante agenda em Manaus.
articles.body:
Professora Maria do Carmo participa de caminhada e promete reforçar efetivo policial no AM. — Foto: g1 AM

A candidata ao governo do Amazonas, Professora Maria do Carmo ( PL ), participou de uma caminhada no bairro Manoa, na Zona Norte de Manaus , na manhã deste sábado (29). Durante a agenda, ela conversou com moradores e apresentou propostas para a área da segurança pública, como a melhoria das condições de trabalho dos policiais e a convocação de aprovados em concursos públicos.

Professora Maria do Carmo disputa o cargo pela coligação “Mudar é Urgente”, formada pelo Partido Liberal (PL). Ela já concorreu a outros cargos. Em 2024, foi candidata a vice-prefeita de Manaus na chapa de Capitão Alberto Neto (PL). Em 2022, concorreu ao cargo de suplente do então candidato Arthur Neto (PSDB).

Entre as propostas para a segurança pública, a candidata destacou a melhoria das condições de trabalho dos policiais, com reajuste da data-base, auxílio-fardamento, auxílio-alimentação e vale-aluguel. Ela também afirmou que pretende convocar candidatos aprovados em concursos e reorganizar a segurança pública no estado.

“Em primeiro lugar, para a segurança pública, a gente tem que melhorar o nosso efetivo. Como? Melhorando para os policiais, que estão com a data-base atrasada desde 2021, auxílio-fardamento que eles não têm, melhorar o auxílio à alimentação, vale-aluguel que eles também estão sem. Sem policial qualificado, bem armado, preparado para enfrentar a criminalidade, a gente não vai ter uma segurança efetiva. Depois, nós vamos começar a chamar os concursados, inclusive aqueles que já estão aptos a assumir”, afirmou.

A agenda da candidata também contou com participação em um evento de jogos e tecnologia pela manhã. À tarde, Maria do Carmo visita o ramal do Pau Rosa e participa de um adesivaço de candidatos proporcionais. À noite, ela participa de reuniões em diferentes bairros da Zona Norte de Manaus.

A campanha eleitoral começou no dia 16 de agosto em todo o país. Os candidatos já podem fazer propaganda nas ruas e na internet. Na TV e no rádio, a propaganda começou nesta sexta-feira (28). O primeiro turno das eleições será no dia 4 de outubro.

articles.title: Lula defende igualdade de gênero em encontro com mulheres em BH | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente candidato à reeleição também falou sobre expectativa da aprovação do fim da escala 6x1 e prometeu investimento em escolas integrais num eventual quarto mandato.
articles.summary: Presidente candidato à reeleição também falou sobre expectativa da aprovação do fim da escala 6x1 e prometeu investimento em escolas integrais num eventual quarto mandato.
articles.body:
Ato "Mulheres com Lula" em Belo Horizonte — Foto: TV Globo/ Reprodução

O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) defendeu igualdade de gênero em cargos de gestão no governo federal e convidou mulheres a votar em mulheres, em evento realizado em Belo Horizonte neste sábado (29). O candidato à reeleição participou de um ato chamado "Mulheres com Lula", com a participação de ministras, senadoras e candidatas de diversos estados do país.

"Participação de mulheres em cargos de gestão: estamos com 38%, e é pouco. Precisamos chegar a 50% ou mais", disse Lula.

O presidente destacou que, embora as mulheres sejam maioria na sociedade brasileira, ainda são minoria no Legislativo.

O Brasil tem 6 milhões de mulheres a mais do que homens , segundo o Censo de 2022. O público feminino corresponde a 52,84% do eleitorado que deve ir às urnas em outubro.

"Democracia é o poder que emana do povo em nome do povo, e veja a contradição, vocês são a maioria. Se todas as mulheres votassem em mulheres, a gente teria no Congresso uma maioria de mulheres. Se vocês votarem em senadoras mulheres, a gente vai ter maioria de senadoras. Por que vocês têm que ser representadas por homens?", questionou.

Além de Lula, o candidato do PT ao governo de Minas Gerais, Patrus Ananias, e o vice dele, Jarbas Soares Júnior (PSB), foram os únicos homens a subirem ao palco do evento. As candidatas ao Senado pelo estado Marília Campos (PT) e Áurea Carolina (PSOL) discursaram para o público feminino.

Lula também falou da expectativa de aprovação da Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) do fim da escala 6x1 pelo Congresso na próxima semana.

Na última quinta-feira (27), o senador Omar Aziz (PSD-AM) entregou à Comissão de Constituição e Justiça (CCJ) do Senado relatório a favor da PEC. A previsão é que o texto seja votado pela CCJ nos próximos dias .

"Nós vamos aprovar nesta semana o fim da escala 6x1 para que as mulheres e os homens tenham mais tempo de cuidar da própria vida, mais tempo de cuidar das crianças, mais tempo para passear e mais tempo para namorar também", disse o presidente.

Lula ainda destacou que, caso seja reeleito, a educação será a primeira prioridade de seu quarto mandato.

"Nós vamos ter que resolver a questão da educação definitivamente. Escola de tempo integral não apenas para a criança ficar o dia inteiro na escola aprendendo arte, cultura, dança, tudo o que ela quiser. Aprendendo política ambiental, aprendendo na escola que homem não é mais forte que mulher, não é mais importante, aprendendo que somos iguais".

articles.title: Lourdes Melo está na UTI após sofrer AVC hemorrágico no Piauí | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a família, ela permanece sob cuidados intensivos e em observação médica.
articles.summary: Lourdes Melo, candidata ao Governo do Piauí pelo PCO, está sob cuidados intensivos em Teresina após sofrer um AVC hemorrágico, mas segue lúcida e estável.
articles.body:
Candidata ao Governo do Piauí, Lourdes Melo (PCO) — Foto: Mayara Valença/g1 Piauí

A candidata ao Governo do Piauí pelo Partido da Causa Operária (PCO), Lourdes Melo, de 73 anos, está lúcida e estável após sofrer um AVC hemorrágico na sexta-feira (28) . A informação foi divulgada pela família na tarde deste sábado (29)

Lourdes está internada na Unidade de Terapia Intensiva (UTI) de um hospital de Teresina . Segundo a família, ela permanece sob cuidados médicos e em observação.

Na quinta-feira (27), a equipe de assessoria do PCO informou que a candidata não teria compromissos de campanha na sexta-feira por motivos de saúde.

Lourdes Melo (PCO) é professora aposentada, sindicalista e militante histórica da esquerda no Piauí. Natural de Pedreiras (MA), vive em Teresina desde a década de 1970 e construiu sua trajetória política nos movimentos sindicais e na defesa da educação pública.

Ela disputou sua primeira eleição em 1992 e, desde então, concorreu diversas vezes a cargos como prefeita, vice-governadora e governadora do Piauí, sem exercer mandato eletivo. Filiada ao PCO desde 2005, tornou-se uma das principais representantes da legenda no estado.

Lourdes ganhou projeção nacional em 2022 após viralizar durante um debate eleitoral e, em 2026, voltou a disputar o Governo do Piauí defendendo pautas voltadas à educação pública, aos direitos dos trabalhadores e aos movimentos populares.

articles.title: Propaganda eleitoral na TV e rádio: Lula e Flávio estreiam peças | G1
articles.standfirst: Peças publicitárias apostam em apresentação dos candidatos aos eleitores e já trazem primeiros ataques a adversários. Propaganda nas redes sociais já está liberada desde o dia 16 de agosto.
articles.summary: A propaganda eleitoral na TV e rádio estreou com Lula focando em propostas, enquanto Flávio Bolsonaro apostou na imagem familiar e Caiado em se apresentar
articles.body:
Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, Augusto Cury e Ronaldo Caiado terão tempo em rádio e TV — Foto: Divulgação

Neste sábado (29), as campanhas dos candidatos à Presidência exibiram os primeiros programas da propaganda eleitoral gratuita no rádio e na TV.

Apenas quatro candidatos têm direito a tempo, conforme a lei eleitoral:

Flávio Bolsonaro (PL): 4 minutos e 20 segundos.

Ronaldo Caiado (PSD): 2 minutos e 2 segundos.

Campanhas apostam em estratégias diferentes

De início, a campanha de Lula destacou a trajetória política e seus mandatos anteriores. Também teve como foco as propostas que são bandeiras do governo, como o fim da escala 6x1, a isenção de imposto de renda para quem ganha até R$ 5 mil e a defesa da soberania.

O programa eleitoral de Lula também ataca Flávio Bolsonaro, seu principal adversário. A propaganda apresenta um "currículo" com críticas ao adversário, com fatos como sua relação com o miliciano Adriano da Nóbrega e o pedido de dinheiro a Daniel Vorcaro, ex-banqueiro investigado por fraudes bilionárias no Banco Master, para financiar o filme "Dark Horse".

Flávio optou por uma abordagem focada na economia e na segurança pública. O candidato do PL se apresenta como "advogado e empresário, casado com a Fernanda, pai da Luísa e da Carol" e faz uma apresentação de seu currículo.

O restante do tempo de seu programa eleitoral é voltado a apresentar sua família, com especial atenção para as mulheres. Flávio tem como um dos objetivos da campanha atrair o voto feminino. Sua mulher, Fernanda, chega a dizer que reeducou e que ele é o "mais moderado dos Bolsonaros".

Caiado, ex-governador de Goiás, também se apresentou ao eleitor no primeiro programa eleitor, mas sem deixar de criticar os governos do PT. O candidato do PSD destacou seus "quarenta anos de vida pública" e a gestão como governador de Goiás.

Augusto Cury se apresentou como um "agente da despolarização" da política. Na peça publicitária, o candidato faz um trocadilho com seu nome e a palavra cura, e diz: "Cury este país".

A propaganda eleitoral gratuita conta com dois blocos de 12 minutos e 30 segundos.

Neste sábado, primeiro dia, os programas são veiculados na seguinte ordem, definida por sorteio pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE): Avante, PSD, PL e Coligação Brasil Pronto pra Mais (PT).

A partir do segundo dia, o sistema será de rodízio: o partido ou coligação que veicular seu programa por último será o primeiro no dia seguinte.

Há revezamento com a propaganda de candidatos a governador, em dias alternados. Parte do tempo é reservada a candidatos a cargos do Legislativo (deputado e senador).

Como funciona a distribuição de propaganda?

Há regras para a distribuição do tempo de propaganda eleitoral gratuita.

10% do tempo é distribuído igualmente entre as siglas que cumprem a cláusula de desempenho (meta de votos que partidos devem atingir para ter acesso ao Fundo Partidário e ao tempo de propaganda — clique para saber mais ).

Os outros 90% são distribuídos proporcionalmente à representação de cada partido na Câmara dos Deputados.

Lula tem o maior tempo porque o PT é uma das maiores bancadas na Câmara e se aliou a PSB, PDT e à federação PSOL/Rede nestas eleições.

Renan Santos (Missão), Romeu Zema (Novo) e os demais candidatos à Presidência não vão aparecer na propaganda porque seus partidos não cumpriram os critérios da clásula de desempenho, mas podem fazer campanha nas redes sociais e nas ruas, o que está liberado desde o dia 16 de agosto.

Veja, a seguir, mais detalhes das primeiras propagandas:

Os materiais de propaganda petista apresentam duas estratégias diferentes da campanha de Lula: reforçar pautas do governo, como o fim da escala 6 x 1, e atacar Flávio Bolsonaro. Em um dos vídeos, o presidente se dirige ao telespectador e diz: "juntos, nós reconstruímos o Brasil. Agora, queremos dar um salto de qualidade, porque o Brasil está pronto para mais".

O início do programa foca em críticas contra Flávio Bolsonaro, citando investigações como o caso das rachadinhas, em que ele foi denunciado em 2020 pelo Ministério Público do Rio de Janeiro por organização criminosa e lavagem de dinheiro. As provas da investigação foram anuladas porque tribunais decidiram que Flávio tinha direito a foro privilegiado, por ser parlamentar. Também há menções ao pedido de dinheiro ao banqueiro preso Daniel Vorcaro, do Master , para financiar o filme "Dark Horse", sobre Jair Bolsonaro. O caso está sob investigação.

Em post nas redes sociais, o Secretário Nacional de Comunicação do PT, Éden Valadares, disse que o início do programa na TV é o momento em que a sociedade começa a prestar atenção nas eleições. "Neste sentido, avaliamos ser importante mostrar quem é Flávio, qual é sua história e apresentar seu currículo", escreveu.

A campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro preparou para a estreia uma propaganda voltada à apresentação do senador. Segundo integrantes da campanha ouvidos pelo g1 , a primeira peça busca retratar o filho mais velho do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro como um "homem de família".

A estratégia foi começar com uma abordagem mais leve e deixar para os programas seguintes ataques mais diretos a Lula, com citações ao caso envolvendo Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, o Lulinha, seu filho mais velho, investigado sob a suspeita de tráfico de influência . A equipe ainda discute em qual momento o assunto será levado ao horário eleitoral.

Nas próximas peças, o senador também deve abordar temas como segurança pública e custo de vida, com foco na perda do poder de compra dos brasileiros. Nas palavras de um interlocutor do candidato: "apresentar o problema e, depois, a solução".

Em dois minutos e dois segundos, o ex-governador escolheu falar de sua trajetória política e de segurança pública.

A campanha associa "coragem" à atuação de Caiado como médico e também no enfrentamento ao PT. A peça faz menção a grupos que invadem terras "de quem plantava". O candidato iniciou sua trajetória política como uma liderança ruralista, ligada ao agronegócio. Foi candidato à Presidência em 1989, e depois deputado, senador e governador.

No decorrer da peça, a campanha cita o casamento de 35 anos com Gracinha Caiado e credita ao candidato o enfrentamento de facções criminosas em Goiás, além de avanços em hospitais, escolas, transporte e inteligência artificial no estado. Na segunda metade, o tom muda com ataques ao PT. A peça diz que há uma crise de segurança no país e atribui a situação a "20 anos" de gestões petistas.

Nos 35 segundos, Cury se coloca como uma opção contra a polarização. O candidato do Avante utiliza clipes de reportagens sobre o escândalo de corrupção conhecido como mensalão e do ataque do 8 de janeiro.

Sem TV, candidatos apostam nas redes sociais

Ao g1 , a coordenadora da campanha de Renan Santos, vereadora Amanda Vettorazzo (União-SP), afirmou que a estratégia é produzir conteúdo para as redes de forma constante e aproveitar a rotina do candidato para fazer as gravações. Segundo ela, Renan grava vídeos durante viagens, eventos e até dentro do carro. "Como a gente não tem tempo de TV, não gravou em estúdio", afirma.

Zema disse na sexta-feira (28) a jornalistas que também aposta na relevância das redes . Segundo ele, a presença nos meios de comunicação tradicionais não é 100% determinante para uma campanha ser bem-sucedida. Em grupos de WhatsApp, membros do partido Novo tentam mobilizar a militância para aumentar a exposição do candidato em vídeos, buscando viralização.

articles.title: Defesa Civil alerta para calor e chuva no interior de SP neste domingo | G1
articles.standfirst: Previsão é de pancadas de chuva rápidas, localizadas e de maior intensidade, principalmente na região de Itapeva.
articles.summary: A Defesa Civil emitiu um alerta para onda de calor e pancadas de chuva neste domingo (30), no interior do estado de São Paulo.
articles.body:
Defesa Civil de SP alerta para calorão e pancadas de chuva durante o final de semana — Foto: Defesa Civil / Divulgação

A Defesa Civil emitiu um alerta para onda de calor e pancadas de chuva neste domingo (30), no interior do estado de São Paulo. A áreapontada com maior risco de tempestades é o Sul paulista, na região de Itapeva (SP).

A orientação do órgão é manter a atenção redobrada, pois a chuva deve vir acompanhada de descargas elétricas e rajadas de vento .

As regiões de Sorocaba , Marília e Presidente Prudente também estão sob alerta para risco de pancadas isoladas de chuva. Já em Bauru , Araçatuba e São José do Rio Preto o aviso é para o tempo seco e as altas temperaturas, que podem chegar a 40 °C.

Diante do calor intenso, o governo estadual reforçou o pedido de cuidado à população para evitar queimadas. A combinação de temperaturas elevadas com a vegetação ressecada aumenta o risco de incêndios.

Para quem trafega pelas rodovias, a principal orientação é não jogar cigarros, fósforos ou qualquer material inflamável pela janela do veículo.

Em situações de emergência, o atendimento pode ser solicitado pelos telefones 199, da Defesa Civil, e 193, do Corpo de Bombeiros.

Para receber alertas gratuitos da Defesa Civil por SMS, cadastre o CEP de interesse enviando uma mensagem de texto para o número 40199.

articles.title: Eleições 2026: Roberto Cidade participa de caminhada e propõe ampliar 'Paredão' para todo o estado | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do União Brasil ao governo do Amazonas participou de caminhada na Zona Leste de Manaus, neste sábado (29), onde apresentou propostas para a segurança pública.
articles.summary: Candidato do União Brasil ao governo do Amazonas participou de caminhada na Zona Leste de Manaus, neste sábado (29), onde apresentou propostas para a segurança pública.
articles.body:
Roberto Cidade participa de caminhada e propõe ampliar ‘Paredão’ em Manaus e interior. — Foto: g1 AM

O candidato ao governo do Amazonas, Roberto Cidade ( União Brasil ), participou de uma caminhada no "rua do Fuxico", no bairro Jorge Teixeira, Zona Leste de Manaus , na manhã deste sábado (29). Durante a agenda, ele falou sobre propostas para a área da segurança pública, como a ampliação do sistema ‘Paredão’, a criação de uma muralha digital e a expansão das ações para os municípios do interior.

Roberto Cidade disputa o cargo pela Federação União Progressista, formada por União Brasil e Progressistas, em coligação com o Podemos e o Partido Socialista Brasileiro ( PSB ). O candidato se tornou governador do Amazonas em maio deste ano, após ser eleito de forma indireta pela Assembleia Legislativa do Amazonas (Aleam).

Entre as propostas para a segurança pública, o candidato destacou a ampliação do sistema ‘Paredão’, a criação de uma muralha digital para monitoramento e o fortalecimento das guardas municipais do interior. Segundo Cidade, a estrutura também será utilizada no combate ao tráfico de drogas.

“Nós vamos ampliar o Paredão, nós vamos fazer a muralha digital e levar para o interior também. Vamos fazer o concurso público, vamos também reafirmar o nosso compromisso de melhorar cada vez mais a estrutura da segurança pública. Nós já entregamos duas lanchas blindadas, vamos entregar mais duas esse ano. Vamos fazer a nossa muralha que vai vir lá da Tríplice Fronteira para cá para a gente continuar fazendo apreensões de drogas e vamos fortalecer toda a guarda municipal”, afirmou.

No fim da manhã, ele participou de um almoço com correligionários na Zona Centro-Sul. A agenda do candidato continua pela tarde com a gravação de programa eleitoral e outra caminhada na Zona Leste. À noite, ele participa de uma reunião política na Zona Sul.

A campanha eleitoral começou no dia 16 de agosto em todo o país. Os candidatos já podem fazer propaganda nas ruas e na internet. Na TV e no rádio, a propaganda começou nesta sexta-feira (28). O primeiro turno das eleições será no dia 4 de outubro.

articles.title: A eleição que resiste a mudar; leia análise de Felipe Nunes | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisas estaduais mostram que, apesar das oscilações locais, a disputa presidencial de 2026 continua organizada em torno dos mesmos polos e da mesma geografia eleitoral de 2022, escreve o diretor da Quaest e professor da Fundação Getúlio Vargas (FGV).
articles.summary: Pesquisas estaduais mostram que, apesar das oscilações locais, a disputa presidencial continua organizada em torno dos mesmos polos e da mesma geografia eleitoral.
articles.body:
As pesquisas estaduais da Quaest divulgadas ao longo desta semana revelam uma eleição que se movimenta pouco onde mais importa.

Há oscilações nas intenções de voto, mudanças de intensidade entre os estados e efeitos produzidos por candidaturas locais. Mas, quando observamos o conjunto, o quadro é de estabilidade. A disputa presidencial de 2026 continua calcificada, polarizada entre Lula e o campo político de Jair Bolsonaro, agora representado por Flávio.

Calcificação não significa que nada muda. Significa que as mudanças acontecem dentro de limites estreitos, sem alterar a estrutura que organiza a escolha dos eleitores. Lula preserva a força no Nordeste. Flávio herda a vantagem bolsonarista no Sul e em parte do Centro-Oeste. São Paulo continua dividido, com inclinação à direita. E Minas Gerais permanece como o estado mais próximo do equilíbrio nacional.

A comparação com 2022 ajuda a dimensionar essa estabilidade. Para fazê-la corretamente, é preciso colocar os dois números na mesma base: a intenção de voto atual deve ser comparada com os votos obtidos em 2022 sobre o total de eleitores aptos, e não com os votos válidos. As pesquisas representam todos os eleitores, inclusive aqueles que poderão se abster ou votar em branco e nulo. Mudar o denominador muda o significado do resultado.

Feito esse ajuste, Lula aparece dentro da margem de erro do seu desempenho de 2022 em 16 das 25 unidades da Federação incluídas na consolidação. Está acima em cinco e abaixo em quatro. Ou seja, em quase dois terços dos estados pesquisados, não há evidência estatística de mudança em relação à eleição passada.

Mesmo as diferenças significativas reforçam a ideia de movimentos regionais, não de uma onda nacional. Lula melhora no Maranhão, em Pernambuco, Sergipe, Rio Grande do Norte e Rondônia. Piora em Minas Gerais, Paraná, Santa Catarina e Rio Grande do Sul. As perdas estão concentradas especialmente no Sul e no estado que decidiu a eleição passada por uma diferença mínima. Os ganhos, por sua vez, aparecem sobretudo em áreas nas quais o petismo já era competitivo ou dominante.

O Nordeste continua sendo o principal pilar eleitoral de Lula. Na Bahia, ele registra 53% das intenções de voto no cenário consolidado, praticamente repetindo o patamar de 2022 quando se considera o total de eleitores aptos. Em Pernambuco, chega a 54%, três pontos acima do desempenho anterior. No Rio Grande do Norte, avança de 49% para 54%. Não se trata apenas de liderança. É a preservação de uma vantagem regional sem a qual Lula dificilmente consegue compensar as derrotas no Sul e em parte do Sudeste.

Desempenho de Lula nos estados no 1° turno — Foto: Reprodução

No outro extremo, Flávio reproduz a geografia eleitoral construída por seu pai. Em Santa Catarina, tem 45% no primeiro turno, contra 20% de Lula. No Paraná, mantém uma vantagem ampla. No Rio Grande do Sul, lidera por 34% a 28%. A intensidade varia de um estado para outro, mas o alinhamento permanece: o Sul continua sendo o território mais favorável ao bolsonarismo.

Nos três maiores colégios eleitorais, a estabilidade assume a forma de equilíbrio. Em São Paulo, Flávio tem 30% e Lula 29%. Em Minas Gerais, são 31% a 30%. No Rio de Janeiro, 31% a 29%. Os números estão dentro das respectivas margens de erro.

Isso significa que, mesmo depois de quatro anos de governo, mudanças econômicas, crises políticas e da substituição de Jair por Flávio Bolsonaro, os dois campos chegam ao início da campanha praticamente nivelados nos estados que concentram a maior parcela do eleitorado.

Soma dos dois primeiros colocados no 1° turno — Foto: Reprodução

Estes são dados de 1º turno, revelam a força base de cada candidato nos diversos estados. Não se deve extrair daqui projeções para a eleição, já que este é o retrato do momento. Tampouco dá para ampliar a análise e considerá-la proporcional ao que pode acontecer no segundo turno. Disputas de segundo turno dependem, em grande medida, de como a eleição termina no primeiro turno.

O dado mais importante talvez seja justamente a capacidade de transferência do voto bolsonarista. Flávio não tem a trajetória nem o grau de relevância nacional do pai. Ainda assim, consegue ocupar o mesmo espaço político e reconstruir boa parte de sua coalizão eleitoral. O sobrenome funciona como um atalho: oferece identidade, organiza adversários e reduz o custo de coordenação da direita. A polarização brasileira depende cada vez menos da presença dos dois personagens originais e cada vez mais das identidades políticas que eles consolidaram.

Isso também ajuda a explicar por que as candidaturas alternativas encontram tanta dificuldade. Somados, Lula e Flávio concentram cerca de 60% das intenções de voto em São Paulo e Minas Gerais, superam esse patamar no Rio de Janeiro e ocupam parcelas ainda maiores nos estados em que um dos dois é dominante. Aos demais candidatos resta disputar um eleitorado menor, menos convicto e frequentemente atraído de volta aos dois polos quando aumenta a percepção de risco eleitoral.

Goiás é a principal exceção. No estado, Ronaldo Caiado consegue transformar a força de seu governo e de sua trajetória local em competitividade presidencial. Ele supera Lula e aparece tecnicamente empatado com Flávio. Mas a exceção goiana também mostra o limite das alternativas: ter força no estado de origem não é o mesmo que construir uma coalizão nacional. Até agora, nenhuma candidatura conseguiu transportar esse desempenho para fora de sua base com intensidade suficiente para reorganizar a eleição.

Por isso, a melhor imagem da disputa não é a de uma fotografia congelada. É a de uma eleição que se move dentro de trilhos já conhecidos. Lula pode ganhar alguns pontos no Nordeste e perder outros no Sul. Flávio pode consolidar a direita e reduzir a distância nacional. Candidatos regionais podem alterar o resultado em seus estados. Mas a estrutura continua a mesma: dois polos fortes, rejeições elevadas e pouco espaço disponível entre eles.

A campanha ainda importa. Ela pode mudar o comparecimento, convencer indecisos e alterar a intensidade com que cada grupo chega às urnas. Em uma disputa equilibrada, pequenas diferenças de mobilização podem decidir o resultado. O que as pesquisas desta semana mostram, porém, é que a campanha começa sem realinhamento eleitoral relevante. O Brasil de 2026 continua dividido, quase nos mesmos lugares e em proporções muito próximas às de 2022.

Essa é a força — e o limite — de uma eleição calcificada. Os eleitores podem mudar de opinião sobre o governo, a economia ou os candidatos. Mas, na hora de escolher entre os dois campos que organizam a política nacional, a maioria continua voltando para o mesmo lado da divisão.

articles.title: The Pentagon’s new nuclear doctrine needs congressional guardrails
articles.summary: Critics in Congress and the arms control community are right: Any doctrine premised on “limited” nuclear use invites the illusion of control.
articles.body:
For more than three decades, American nuclear strategy rested on the assumption that U.S. weapons capable of ending civilization several times over would deter adversaries from crossing the nuclear threshold. That assumption is now being tested.

According to NBC News , and broadly confirmed by Undersecretary of Defense for Policy Elbridge Colby, the Department of Defense is drafting a nuclear strategy that places far greater weight on shorter-range, lower-yield tactical weapons in a regional conflict with Russia or China.

This is not, as Moscow’s and Beijing’s propagandists claim, a march toward nuclear war. It is an acknowledgment that America’s deterrent has a credibility gap, and that gap has been widening for years.

Here’s the uncomfortable part: the logic behind the reassessment is sound. America’s current posture forces any president into a binary choice — absorb a limited nuclear strike on an ally or retaliate in a way that risks Armageddon.

Vladimir Putin’s generals have spent two decades developing an “escalate to de-escalate” doctrine, using small battlefield nuclear weapons to shock NATO into freezing a conflict, betting Washington would blink rather than trade New York for Warsaw. Beijing has built a rapidly expanding force of theater-range missiles capable of similar coercive signaling against Taiwan and Japan. If Washington’s only response to a tactical provocation is total strategic war, its deterrent deters very little.

Colby has been walking a careful line. At STRATCOM’s Deterrence Symposium in Omaha this month, he called the effort a “ relook ” at deployment guidance rather than a policy announcement. Days later he went the other way, telling reporters the goal is “to maintain deterrence and stability rather than to exacerbate it.” Either way, the review is real, and the politics are already delicate.

None of this is new territory. In the 1980s, NATO’s Euromissile deployments were justified on identical grounds that a Soviet strike on Europe could not be met solely by threatening an intercontinental exchange. That deployment sparked mass protests yet arguably brought Moscow to the table for the Intermediate-range Nuclear Forces Treaty . Firmness, not restraint, produced that breakthrough.

There is real danger here. Critics in Congress and the arms control community are right: Any doctrine premised on “limited” nuclear use invites the illusion of control. War games suggest a tactical exchange that, once begun, is exceedingly difficult to contain. The fog of war does not respect neat escalation ladders.

The timing compounds the risk. The New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty (New START) lapsed in February . For the first time in more than half a century, no treaty ceiling restrains Washington’s or Moscow’s deployed warheads, strategic or tactical. A doctrine expanding the perceived usability of nuclear weapons, unaccompanied by any arms control framework, risks triggering the buildup Russian and Chinese state media are already highlighting as proof of American “ nuclear blackmail ”.

That criticism should be read for what it is: an attempt to deter Washington from closing its own credibility gap. Dmitriy Trenin, president of the Russian International Affairs Council has warned expanded U.S. tactical deployments would sharply raise tensions — a remarkable complaint from the nation that pioneered modern tactical nuclear coercion in Europe.

Beijing’s Global Times has denounced the review as coercive pressure, even as China’s stockpile has grown from roughly 200 warheads a decade ago to about 620 today, by independent estimates , with the Pentagon projecting up to 1,500 by 2035 — still well short of Washington’s roughly 3,700 and Moscow’s roughly 4,400. That trajectory looks less like a bid for parity with the U.S. or Russia than a deterrence posture calibrated against them.

Toward its neighbors, though, an arsenal that size is unambiguously offensive-capable, and Beijing is already fielding theater-range systems aimed at Taiwan’s American guarantors. Washington isn’t creating a new category of nuclear risk. It’s catching up to one its rivals built while American doctrine stood still.

The path forward requires discipline. Any expansion of tactical options must be married to ironclad command-and-control safeguards, so flexibility doesn’t curdle into the ambiguity critics fear. Washington must treat this posture shift as leverage, not an end in itself. It’s worth more if it eventually forces Moscow and Beijing toward a negotiated framework than if it becomes the new steady state of an unconstrained arms race.

And allied consultation cannot be an afterthought. Poland, the Baltic states, South Korea and Japan will each weigh reassurance against the anxiety of becoming a bigger target. NATO’s Nuclear Planning Group and equivalent Indo-Pacific consultations need to be brought in early — and for real.

There is also a domestic dimension. For those worried about rising right-wing populism worldwide, a safer security environment under a rejuvenated American nuclear umbrella is more likely to bolster liberal democratic institutions than undermine them.

Colby is not manufacturing a crisis. He’s responding to one Moscow and Beijing have been building for years while Washington’s tactical deterrent atrophied. The Pentagon is right to close that gap. But credibility bought through expanded nuclear options is only durable if it’s disciplined and transparent to allies and aimed at restoring the negotiated stability that ended the last Cold War.

Washington should not trade one credibility gap for a far more dangerous one.

Ariel Cohen, Ph.D. is a senior fellow (non-resident) at the Atlantic Council’s Eurasia Center and Global Energy Center, and director of the Energy, Growth and Security Program at the International Tax and Investment Center. He is the founding principal of International Market Analysis.

articles.title: Pennsylvania commissioner accuses Shapiro of 'deceptive' measles death framing as RFK Jr blasts Dem governor
articles.summary: Lancaster County Commissioner Joshua Parsons accuses Gov. Josh Shapiro of deception over measles-related deaths, saying the coroner has no record of them.
articles.body: A Pennsylvania county commissioner is challenging Gov. Josh Shapiro’s announcement of two measles-associated deaths, fueling a growing clash with Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. as the state’s outbreak swells to 460 confirmed cases across 31 counties. Joshua Parsons, one of three Lancaster County commissioners, accused Shapiro of being intentionally "deceptive" during a press conference earlier this week, when the Democratic governor pointed to two "measles-related deaths" in the county. "Well, the governor, in the press conference, they said they were measles-associated deaths, but it was framed, and very much the underlying assertion to it, was that these were measles deaths," Parsons told Fox News Digital. During a Tuesday press conference alongside Dr. Debra Bogen at Penn Medicine Lancaster General Health Hospital, Shapiro announced the deaths of two people who were unvaccinated for measles. "Today, we see the consequences of a lack of immunizations in the first measles-associated deaths that our Commonwealth has seen in 35 years," Shapiro said. FORMER CDC ADVISER SAYS DECLINE IN KINDERGARTEN VACCINATIONS NOTHING TO WORRY ABOUT: 'KEEP CALM AND CARRY ON' Shapiro strongly urged Pennsylvanians to get vaccinated for measles during the press conference. "I want to be clear: This illness and death from measles is completely preventable," he said. Parsons said Shapiro cast the deaths as being the result of measles. MEASLES DEATHS MAY HAVE BEEN 'FABRICATED,' RFK JR CLAIMS AFTER CORONER RAISES QUESTIONS Parsons noted that national media outlets framed the deaths as being from measles. The New York Times, in a Tuesday story still posted to its website, wrote the headline, "Two Unvaccinated People Died From Measles in Pennsylvania, Officials Say." MEASLES DEATHS MAY HAVE BEEN 'FABRICATED,' RFK JR CLAIMS AFTER CORONER RAISES QUESTIONS However, according to conversations he had with the Lancaster County Coroner, Parsons claimed nobody in the county has died from measles this year. "The coroner reported that they don't have… they had zero measles deaths or measles associated-deaths reported. And in Pennsylvania if you have someone who dies of a contagious disease, that does have to be reported to the county coroner," Parsons told Fox News Digital. MEASLES DEATHS MAY HAVE BEEN 'FABRICATED,' RFK JR CLAIMS AFTER CORONER RAISES QUESTIONS The coroner, Dr. Stephen Diamoantoni, has also publicly stated in interviews with local media that he had not been contacted by either Shapiro or the Pennsylvania Department of Health and was surprised to learn of the press conference. "The coroner had one case where there was an infant who died in a home birth, and he's talked about this publicly, and that infant died with measles but not of measles. At the time of the press conference, the state did not indicate who these two cases were or anything about them. Subsequently, they came out and said that this infant is one of the ones they're counting," Parsons told Fox News Digital. MEASLES DEATHS MAY HAVE BEEN 'FABRICATED,' RFK JR CLAIMS AFTER CORONER RAISES QUESTIONS The Pennsylvania Department of Health, in a statement to Fox News Digital, asserted that it consistently referred to the cases as "measles-associated." "PA DOH did not describe the cause of death of either individual. As PA DOH has repeatedly made clear since Tuesday, the Department consistently used the term ‘measles-associated’ in relation to these two deaths. That term means laboratory or epidemiologic evidence of measles is present — in both cases there was a positive measles test — but the disease may not be assessed by the medical certifier or coroner to be the immediate cause of death," the statement read. MEASLES DEATHS MAY HAVE BEEN 'FABRICATED,' RFK JR CLAIMS AFTER CORONER RAISES QUESTIONS The coroner did acknowledge the presence of measles in the infant who died, but said neither he nor the pathologist who examined the infant believed measles to be the cause of death. The coroner, according to Parsons, said the infant died of a lacerated spleen. He also said he has received no information about the second person mentioned by Shapiro and the Pennsylvania Department of Health. MEASLES DEATHS MAY HAVE BEEN 'FABRICATED,' RFK JR CLAIMS AFTER CORONER RAISES QUESTIONS Parsons said that suggested the deaths not being from measles. "The Health Department put out a statement in reply to some of these questions. And I think it just raised more questions, but one line they had in there was that not all deaths in Pennsylvania have to be reported to the county coroner, and that's true. If you have, for example, an elderly person who dies of natural causes, that does not have to be investigated or reported to the coroner," Parsons said. "But if you have someone who dies of an infectious disease, that does have to be reported. So if there is a second death in Lancaster County, that should have been reported," Parsons said. "Now, there's an unlikely scenario that someone contracted measles here and then died outside the county, and that would be reported to another county coroner. And if that's the case, which I think is highly unlikely, if it is the case, they should state that." The Pennsylvania Department of Health, in response to Fox News Digital asking the department why it did not contact the coroner, said "Pennsylvania Statutes Title 16 (Pennsylvania Statutes Title 16 P.S. Counties § 4236 | FindLaw) outlines when a coroner would be called in to investigate a death. While DOH collaborates with county coroners in various ways, including death reporting, DOH does not regulate or oversee coroner operations, nor are coroners involved in most deaths within their county. " Kennedy was also critical of Shapiro’s comments. "Governor Shapiro's unseemly rush to Lancaster County to convene a national press conference and his giddy delight in announcing two measles deaths was a morose commentary on the contemporary political dialogue," Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. wrote in a Wednesday post on X. "The performance was a replay of the Democrats' COVID playbook: fearmongering, misinformation, finger-pointing, and the weaponization of infectious disease fears for political gain," his post continued. "The announcement appears to have been premature, and the deaths may even have been altogether fabricated by one of the Governor's hopeful staffers. The Lancaster County Coroner says that it has no record of any measles deaths. State law requires that all measles deaths be reported to the coroner," Kennedy also added. Kennedy and Shapiro, according to The Washington Post, had a heated phone call just minutes before Shapiro’s Tuesday announcement. During the call, Shapiro reportedly told Kennedy he did not want the federal government’s help with the ongoing measles outbreak. As of Friday, the Pennsylvania Department of Health said 460 measles cases have been confirmed across 31 counties in the state so far in 2026. It marks the nation’s largest measles outbreak since 1991, according to data from the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The majority of infected persons in the state are not vaccinated, according to the Pennsylvania Department of Health. Parsons highlighted that much of the outbreak is relegated to religious communities whose members choose not to get vaccinated. "There's certainly measles here," Parsons told Fox News Digital. "There are in other Pennsylvania counties as well. And a lot of the focus has been on the plain population, Amish and Mennonites. Many of them choose not to get vaccinated. And by and large, they're going about their life and they're living their life and just continue on. So, we certainly have resources available for people if they wanna get vaccinated, but I believe strongly that's each individual's choice," Parsons concluded. In response to a request for comment, Shapiro’s office referred Fox News Digital to the Pennsylvania Department of Health. Reached by Fox News Digital, a representative from the Times said the newspaper is "confident in the accuracy of our story." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fox News Digital also contacted the White House and the Department of Health and Human Services for additional comment.

articles.title: House Republican aims to put Democrats on the record over DSA with resolution condemning socialism
articles.summary: Jeff Crank's House resolution condemning socialism cites Zohran Mamdani's NYC mayoral win and the DSA's growing political momentum nationwide.
articles.body: Rep. Jeff Crank, R-Colo., introduced a measure Thursday condemning socialism in all its forms, telling Fox News Digital he wants to use the vote to force moderate House Democrats to take a more public stance against the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA). "I keep hearing people like Hakeem Jeffries and others in the Congress saying that they oppose the DSA. Let's see if they're willing to vote for a resolution that would oppose them," Crank told Fox News Digital in an interview on Friday. Crank's House resolution cites New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s victory as one of the clearest signposts of the DSA’s growing political momentum. A recent Brookings Institution analysis found that as of August 12, 123 candidates endorsed or recommended by national, state or local DSA chapters had won primaries this cycle. Most were running for local or state-level office. FAR-LEFT SURGE: MAMDANI-BACKED CANDIDATES OUST DEM ESTABLISHMENT INCUMBENTS Crank described the DSA movement as "anti-American" and "anti-Constitution," arguing that its members are often hostile to free speech, one of the core rights protected by the U.S. Constitution. He also accused DSA members of being anti-Semitic in their advocacy against Israel, particularly after the Oct. 7, 2023, terrorist attacks in Israel. "I would almost say the DSA in some ways is the marriage between socialism, the traditional socialism of Bernie Sanders, and the anti-Semitism of this sort of radical Arab movement," Crank said. He continued: "If that's a marriage, their child is violence, right? It's violence and intimidation. It's showing up at town hall meetings and trying to shout elected officials down, which, by the way, is completely anti-democratic." MAMDANI FACES QUESTIONS OVER TIES TO OUTLET ACCUSED OF ANTISEMITIC TROPES One recent example of DSA members disrupting an elected official came in February, when San Francisco DSA led a protest at a news conference held by Mayor Daniel Lurie, who is Jewish. Lurie was announcing a tax-cut proposal when demonstrators repeatedly chanted "Tax the rich." During the disruption, a woman also shouted "tax the Jews," though DSA and other protesters said she was not affiliated with the group. Crank also took aim at several proposals contained in the DSA's national program, arguing that they undermine "free and fair elections." His House resolution calls for passage of the SAVE Act — which would require proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections — while also highlighting the DSA's support for extending voting rights to "noncitizens." According to the DSA's program, all permanent U.S. residents should have the right to vote, as should incarcerated people and those with criminal convictions. CLINTON-APPOINTED JUDGE TRIGGERS APPEAL AFTER BLOCKING KEY VOTER CITIZENSHIP LAW The program also calls for abolishing the Senate and replacing the Supreme Court with "a judiciary chosen by and subordinate to Congress." Crank also criticized the DSA's explicit opposition to capitalism, arguing that socialism has repeatedly failed both in the United States and abroad. "I find it ironic that many of the people who are pushing socialism or who are involved in the DSA movement, they're people who came here from a different country and now they come here and want to impose... the socialism that they left, that didn't work," Crank said. He singled out Mamdani as "the first verified failure of socialism," citing his pied-à-terre tax. DSA CO-CHAIR PUSHES BACK ON SOVIET UNION COMPARISONS, WANTS PRISONS TO BE 'LESS NECESSARY' "You're seeing socialism at its worst in places like New York with Mamdani who's saying, 'Well, I am just going to tax anybody who has a big house here,'" Crank said. "Well, people can choose to not have a house in New York. So they leave. It doesn't work." He added: "He's the first one to sort of get elected, and now he's trying to spread it and get other DSA members around the country elected." Crank also mentioned Melat Kiros, a 29-year-old DSA member who won her Colorado primary in July after handily defeating Democratic incumbent Diana DeGette. "[Kiros] said America deserved 9/11. So tell me why that's different? When you have a bunch of terrorists on September 11th killing Americans because of ideology, how is that different than what Mao did? It isn't. This is the insidiousness of this movement," Crank said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Crank's resolution similarly draws a line between modern Democratic socialists and past communist regimes under leaders such as Mao Zedong and Joseph Stalin, asserting that socialism has led to famine, mass killings and more than 100 million deaths worldwide. Kiros' comments on 9/11 stem from an interview she did on June 22 with 9News journalist Kyle Clark, who asked her whether she believed the attacks were an "inevitable consequence" of American intervention. "Inevitable in the sense that we destabilized a lot of the Middle East, which led people to believe that another act of violence was the only response. And again, just like I said before, our responsibility is to get rid of those conditions that lead to violence in the first place," Kiros said. Crank's resolution will be considered by the House Rules Committee on Monday, and there will be a vote likely sometime next week, the congressman told Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Trump touts access to 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil in deal he says will slash gas prices
articles.summary: The Trump administration is touting the oil deal with Venezuela as a way to lower gasoline prices, which have been elevated since the Iran war broke out.
articles.body: President Donald Trump on Friday touted an agreement with Venezuela that he said would lower gas prices by giving the U.S. majority control over 65 billion barrels of oil from the South American country's proven reserves. The breakthrough comes as disruptions to global energy markets from the Iran war continue to push up prices at the pump, with Americans now paying an average of $4.08 per gallon for regular gasoline, up from $3.20 a year ago, according to AAA. The agreement with Venezuela will give the U.S. a 55% effective interest in the output of a new private company formed to manage the reserves, a U.S. official familiar with the deal told The Associated Press. While the U.S. will not immediately gain access to 35.75 billion barrels of oil, the 55% interest applies to the oil ultimately produced by the 17 Venezuelan fields covered by the agreement. TRUMP PREDICTS GAS PRICES WILL GO DOWN TO $2.50 PER GALLON IF STRAIT OF HORMUZ FULLY OPENS The agreement also allows the U.S. to purchase Venezuelan oil at cost, a provision that could give American buyers access to cheaper crude once production from the fields increases. The deal is unlikely to translate into an immediate drop in U.S. gasoline prices, however, because experts have said bringing significantly more Venezuelan crude to market will require years of infrastructure work and billions of dollars in investment, according to the AP. Rystad Energy, an independent energy research firm, said in July that Venezuelan oil production could jump 17% by 2028, but only if significant advances are made. According to the firm's report, Venezuela will need "higher drilling activity, extensive workover campaigns, improved infrastructure and significantly greater rig availability." Since much of Venezuela’s crude is extremely heavy and viscous, the country also needs a steady supply of diluents — lighter hydrocarbons blended with the crude to make it thin enough to flow through pipelines and reach refineries and export terminals. In 2021, S&P Global described Venezuelan oil as having "the viscosity of asphalt." TRUMP BLASTS BIG OIL FOR ‘MAKING TOO MUCH MONEY’ The U.S. Energy Information Administration has also previously weighed in on Venezuela's troubled oil industry. In October 2023, after the Biden administration lifted most U.S. sanctions on Venezuela's oil sector, the agency said "years of underinvestment and mismanagement" would limit growth. The Trump administration, however, is betting that U.S. involvement and a massive influx of private investment can reverse the decline. Trump said Friday the new agreement would greatly increase the U.S. oil supply and "substantially lower Gas Prices for all Americans, long into the future." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Secretary of State Marco Rubio similarly said the deal would bring nearly $100 billion in private investment to Venezuela and lower gas prices in the United States. U.S. oil companies have been cautious about investing in Venezuela, citing the country’s deteriorated infrastructure and uncertain business environment. Days after the Trump administration ousted Nicolás Maduro, Trump met with oil executives to discuss potential investment in Venezuela’s energy sector, but several expressed reservations. ExxonMobil CEO Darren Woods said at the time that he viewed Venezuela as "un-investable." The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: German AfD youth group eyes euro stance at congress ahead of key polls
articles.summary: The youth wing of the Alternative for Germany party met for a national congress on Saturday, ahead of a key election in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt th...
articles.body:
The youth wing of the Alternative for Germany party met for a national congress on Saturday, ahead of a key election in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt that could see the far-right AfD take power for the first time.

At the event in the eastern city of Magdeburg, the Generation Deutschland (GD) youth organization discussed its stance on European policy, aiming to distance itself from the main party's line.

Its lead candidate for the Saxony-Anhalt election, Ulrich Siegmund, was met with energetic approval by the delegates.

The approximately 300 participants discussed a statement at the 'Altes Theater' theatre in Magdeburg.

A draft of the statement, which had been made public beforehand, stated that the euro had strengthened the single market but had significant structural flaws. For this reason, they were open to proposals for reform. There is no talk of leaving the euro.

GD leader Jean-Pascal Hohm said that he personally was firmly convinced that Germany should not leave the euro.

However, Hohm ultimately withdrew the relevant motion put forward by the GD leadership after it became clear from speeches that there was significant resistance within the AfD Youth to such a stance.

The AfD was founded in 2013 as a Eurosceptic party. In its 2025 Bundestag election manifesto, it had reaffirmed that "Germany must leave the euro system."

Hohm justified his stance by referring to the way of life of young people, who are used to no longer having to show a passport at borders or convert currencies, he said in remarks to dpa.

'Millions must leave this country again'

At its meeting, the GD appeared extremely self-assured and reiterated calls for mass deportations. "Germany must remain the land of the Germans. This principle is non-negotiable," Hohm asserted. Millions had entered the country, he claimed. "Millions must leave this country again."

Hohm also called on members to defend themselves physically in the event of physical attacks by political opponents.

He does not expect anyone to allow themselves to be "beaten up by violence-seeking anti-fascists or chased through the city" because of their political convictions.

Anyone who defends themselves in a situation of self-defence has the backing of the GD and the parent party. "We are not victims, and we will not allow ourselves to be made into victims."

The GD, which is closely linked to its parent party, was newly founded in Giessen last year after the former AfD youth organization, the Junge Alternative (JA), had been dissolved. The JA was a largely independent association over which the AfD had only limited control.

The meeting was heavily influenced by the election campaign. Referring to the upcoming state election on September 6, Hohm said that history could be made in Saxony-Anhalt next week.

Siegmund, who arrived in the afternoon, was celebrated like a pop star. "The people are on our side," he called out to the participants.

He said he had often heard the word "hope" in recent weeks. "We will make history here in Saxony-Anhalt one way or another."

Siegmund emphasized that he remained optimistic even if the AfD were to fall short of the absolute majority it was aiming for. "Then it'll work out soon in Thuringia, then in Brandenburg, then in Saxony," he called out to the cheering hall.

According to a spokesman, 480 participants, guests and journalists were invited to GD's second national congress.

The police put the number of the group's own participants at 300, while counter-demonstrations on Saturday remained limited in scale, with the police citing around 250 participants before the start of the event.

There were no significant counterdemonstrations of the sort that took place when the GD was founded last year in Giessen.

According to the police, a total of around 600 people took part in demonstrations and rallies against the Federal Congress, the AfD and racism throughout the day at various locations across the city. From the police's point of view, everything remained peaceful.

Due to their anti-constitutional views, the AfD chapters in Saxony-Anhalt and three other eastern states - Thuringia, Saxony and Brandenburg - are classified as "confirmed" right-wing extremist movements by intelligence agencies, allowing for the party to be monitored by authorities.

Nevertheless, the party has soared in popularity in recent years, benefiting from discontent with the political establishment in Berlin, and it is polling above 40% in Saxony-Anhalt ahead of the vote on September 6.

All mainstream parties refuse to work with the AfD, a policy famously known as the "firewall," but successive governments have rejected calls for the party to be banned due to its extremist positions.

articles.title: Dem House hopeful’s delayed disclosure reveals mystery payments from Soros-linked groups
articles.summary: Rebecca Cooke's financial disclosure reveals she was compensated by two organizations with direct ties to George Soros' Open Society Foundation.
articles.body: A waitress running for Congress in Wisconsin's third district was on the payroll of two left-leaning organizations with ties to billionaire investor George Soros' Open Society Foundation. Rebecca Cooke has portrayed herself as a working-class outsider, touting her experience as a waitress, small-business owner and nonprofit leader raised on a dairy farm. But a personal financial disclosure released two days after Wisconsin’s Aug. 13 primary shows she received more than $5,000 apiece for work with Third Way and the Pipeline Fund, two left-leaning organizations with financial ties to George Soros’ Open Society network. The Open Society network awarded $1 million to Third Way’s nonprofit research arm between 2023 and 2024, while the Pipeline Fund received $1.4 million directly from the Open Society Action Fund in 2024. Through the Open Society Foundation, which serves as the umbrella organization for Soros' philanthropy network, Soros has distributed tens of millions of dollars to nonprofits and groups championing left-leaning causes like policing reform, LGBTQ rights and drug decriminalization. Soros has donated more than $32 billion of his personal fortune to the Open Society's Foundation, which has been overseen by his son Alex Soros since 2022. DEMOCRATIC GROUP LAUNCHES $15M WAR ON DSA AFTER SOCIALIST PRIMARY WINS: 'MORTAL DANGER' The financial disclosure forms only report that the amount of money Cooke received from each organization was above $5,000, but they do not specify the exact amount. The personal financial disclosure form covered Jan. 1, 2025, through July 14, 2026. A spokesperson for Third Way confirmed with Fox News Digital reporting by the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel that Cooke received $30,000 in payment "for a project focused on elevating the voices and concerns of working-class Americans that have too often been missing from the rooms where decisions are made." The Foundation to Promote Open Society, a grant making arm of George Soros’ Open Society Foundations network, donated a $500,000 grant to the Third Way Institute in 2023 and another one in 2024, according to IRS-derived grant records. Third Way Institute serves as the 501(c) research arm of the Third Way. In 2024, Third Way Institute transferred $21.9 million to Third Way, accounting for roughly 98% of the institute’s total spending that year. The institute said the money was used to support charitable and educational work on economic, national security, energy and social policy issues. SOROS NETWORK REBUILDS PROGRESSIVE PROSECUTOR PUSH AFTER STRING OF ELECTION LOSSES Fox News Digital reached out to Third Way for comment. Pipeline Fund is a organization that works to train, recruit and support progressive candidates running in state and local election races. It began operating independently in 2024 after spinning off from the Sixteen Thirty Fund, a liberal nonprofit network that has received tens of millions of dollars from the Soros-founded Open Society network. Tax records also show that the Pipeline Fund received $1.4 million directly from the Open Society Action Fund and approximately $2.26 million from the Sixteen Thirty Fund in 2024. Scattered across the country, Pipeline Fund has a network of campaign consulting groups, including one in Wisconsin known as Wisconsin Progress. "We can confirm Rebecca Cooke worked as a contractor for The Pipeline Fund in 2025 to help advance our mission of building a reflective democracy where working-class people, women, people of color, and other underrepresented communities are fully supported to run for office and advance the needs of their communities," Pipeline Fund said in an emailed statement to the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel. HOUSE DEMOCRATS' CAMPAIGN ARM DRAWS PROGRESSIVE FURY FOR TRYING TO 'TIP THE SCALES' IN KEY HOUSE PRIMARY Prior to making a bid for Congress herself, Cooke opened up her own Democratic campaign consulting firm in 2015, in which she worked with eight state and federal campaigns from 2015 to 2021. "Radical Rebecca Cooke is a paid political operative for far-left liberals and wants to push their socialist agenda. Commie Cooke may fit in at [a] Soros-funded consulting firm, but she is far too extreme to represent western Wisconsin," National Republican Congressional Committee spokesman Zach Bannon said in a statement to Fox News Digital. Cooke’s personal financial disclosure was not released until two days after the Aug. 13 primary, following an extension she requested from the clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives in April. All candidates who spend or raise more than $5,000 for a House of Representatives race must submit a personal financial disclosure form 30 days before the election. Rep. Derrick Van Orden, R-Wis., blasted Cooke's delay in releasing her financial records, saying it tells voters all they need to know about her. "For months, Democrats and Republicans across the Third District called on Cooke to release her financial disclosures. She had every opportunity to be transparent with voters. Instead, she chose to keep them hidden until after the primary," Van Orden said in a news release. DEMOCRAT ESTABLISHMENT STRIKES BACK AS SOCIALIST CANDIDATE DOWNED IN BATTLEGROUND PRIMARY "That tells Wisconsin voters everything they need to know about Rebecca Cooke’s character. She was willing to deceive her own party to protect the political persona she built and gain political power," Van Orden said. But Cooke said her financial forms reveal that she truly is a working-class American. "I’ve always worn multiple hats to make ends meet and in addition to waitressing I worked on two projects related to getting more working class people to run for office and conducted research for an organization about how to better connect with working class voters," Cooke said in an email to the Sentinel. "There are unique challenges to running for office as a working class person with an hourly wage job and a full-time campaign schedule. For example, I’m one of the thousands of people in this district who can’t afford health insurance. I’ve been proud to help make it easier for the next generation of working class leaders to step up and take our fight to Washington D.C." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fox News Digital reached to Open Society Foundation, Cooke's campaign and Pipeline Fund for comment.

articles.title: Abdul El-Sayed plays down Hasan Piker ties after streamer’s viral antisemitism firestorm
articles.summary: Abdul El-Sayed tried to downplay his ties to Hasan Piker on air, but Katy Tur pressed him on why he won't fully disassociate ahead of a tight race.
articles.body: Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed tried to turn the page on his ties to controversial streamer Hasan Piker Friday — but MS NOW host Katy Tur pushed back. The candidate’s comments come just days after Piker suggested Jewish Americans are "making antisemitism worse" by voicing their support of Israel — a statement that drew harsh criticism from El-Sayed, who has appeared alongside Piker on the campaign trail. "I believe all Americans deserve the right to advocate for what they believe without fear of violence. This is particularly true for communities that have been intimidated for their beliefs in the past," El-Sayed said in a statement following Piker’s remarks. EL-SAYED DISTANCES HIMSELF FROM HASAN PIKER AFTER DISTURBING REMARKS ABOUT JEWISH AMERICANS He added that "Antisemitism is a scourge, and we need to address it in all its forms," while promising to "stand against any rhetoric that puts the community at risk." "And while politicians and pundits try to make this race about a Twitch streamer, we’re going to be talking about gas, groceries, good schools and healthcare," El-Sayed continued. MICHIGAN DEMOCRAT DEMANDS REPORTERS STOP ASKING 'ABOUT HASAN PIKER' AHEAD OF SENATE RACE On Friday’s "The Moment with Katy Tur," El-Sayed appeared to continue his effort to distance himself from Piker in light of his controversial remarks. "So, if you have Jewish voters in Michigan — I’ll say [Attorney General] Dana Nessel is one of them — who are worried about your association with Hasan Piker. Why? Why keep him so close? Or why not fully disassociate yourself with him, especially when Michigan is so tight? Elissa Slotkin only won by 22,000 votes," Tur asked. According to Ballotpedia, Slotkin won by 19,000 votes. MICHIGAN DEM AG TURNS ON EL-SAYED OVER TERROR ATTACK RESPONSE, WARNS OF MENTALITY THAT 'BOTHERS ME A LOT' "This campaign is not about a streamer in California. This campaign is about affordability in Michigan. This campaign is about the ability to have healthcare," El-Sayed said. Tur pushed back, arguing the "streamer in California does campaign with a lot of Democrats. So he’s not just a streamer." HASAN PIKER IS BECOMING THE 'FACE OF THE PROGRESSIVE MOVEMENT,' FORMER DEMOCRATIC OPERATIVE WARNS El-Sayed appeared to continue distancing himself from Piker, despite Tur’s pushback. "This campaign is about the challenges Michiganders face," El-Sayed continued. "And I get that, in the media, it’s a lot easier to pick up one person and be like, ‘This is what this is about.’ But this is why a lot of people get so frustrated about politics and political media, because it doesn’t actually speak to the challenges they face." WISCONSIN DEMOCRAT DOWNPLAYS APPEARING ON HASAN PIKER'S SHOW, DOESN'T 'ENDORSE' EVERYTHING HE SAYS The exchange continued, with Tur rejecting El-Sayed’s characterization of his public ties to Piker. "It’s not just the media, and I reject that framing," Tur said. "It’s — six in 10 Americans don’t know who he is, and I’m not saying he’s the most important person in the world. But when you have a state like Michigan, where, again, Elissa Slotkin only won by 22,000 votes, is it worth potentially losing the few votes you need to win?" "Ten in 10 Americans agree that they can’t afford the things that they need in their lives," El-Sayed replied. "So, if folks want to make this about a streamer in California, they’re welcome to do that. But I’m focused on Donald Trump. I’m focused on addressing the affordability crisis. I’m focused on getting you healthcare. And that’s what I’m going to stay focused on." FETTERMAN 'DARES' EL-SAYED TO STICK WITH PIKER, CLAIMS MICHIGAN NOMINEE HAS 'LITTLE MAN SYNDROME ENERGY' El-Sayed’s apparent distance himself from Piker drew criticism from Jason Mudd, CEO of Axia Public Relations, who told Fox News Digital his attempts to distance himself from Piker could do more harm than good to his campaign. "Distancing yourself from someone’s comments rarely works," Mudd said. "Owning your own position does. The moment a candidate argues about how close a relationship is, the audience stops listening to the substance and starts watching the deflection." ABDUL EL-SAYED SAYS RALLYING WITH HASAN PIKER DOESN'T MEAN HE ENDORSES 'AMERICA DESERVED 9/11' REMARK "If this were my client, I would advise them to skip the minimizing and go straight to a clear, standalone statement: here’s what I believe, separate from what anyone else said," Mudd continued. "Ambiguity is what keeps a story alive, not the original comment." Mudd added that El-Sayed’s strategy should be to double-down on his own campaign promises and personal beliefs, instead of just claiming he disagrees with Piker’s statements. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE "The test isn’t whether a candidate can prove distance from a controversial figure," Mudd told Fox News Digital. "It’s whether their own answer sounds confident, consistent, and complete the first time. Reporters don’t stop asking follow-up questions. Vague answers do." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP When reached for comment by Fox News Digital, a representative for El-Sayed pointed to a story in The Hill reporting that the candidate has "no plans" to campaign with Piker. Fox News Digital reached out to Piker for comment.

articles.title: Seneca Nation leader calls Trump's Lake America renaming 'unpresidential,' demands reversal
articles.summary: Seneca Nation's leader calls Trump's Lake Ontario to Lake America renaming "unpresidential," saying it violates the 1794 Canandaigua treaty.
articles.body: A day after President Donald Trump signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario "Lake America" amid a trade war with Canada, the leader of Seneca Nation of Indians asked him to reverse it. Calling his order "unpresidential," president J. Conrad Seneca on Friday wrote: "The President cannot assert ownership over our culture or erase it through irresponsible political action. His order should be rescinded, and the name Lake Ontario should be left as it is, reflective of the Seneca people, other Haudenosaunee nations and all Indigenous people surrounding the lake." Seneca explained that the lake derived its name from Indigenous roots. TRUMP TAUNTS CANADA ON RENAMING LAKE ONTARIO THE 'LAKE AMERICA' AMID RISING BORDER TRADE RIFT "In our traditional Seneca language, its name is sga:nyodai:yoh, meaning ‘beautiful lake,’" he wrote in a message shared in the nation’s newsletter. "Long before the United States existed, and before settlers brought the English language to our lands, our Seneca and Haudenosaunee ancestors traveled Lake Ontario and surrounding waterways for many reasons, including diplomacy among our nations. Now, we are seeing the exact opposite of diplomacy." He added that to the people of Seneca Nation, Lake America is not a "political pawn" but rather land that Indigenous people have lived on for thousands of years. HILLARY CLINTON'S DIG AT TRUMP OVER LAKE ONTARIO NAME CHANGE SPARKS VIRAL BACKLASH: 'SHOOTING BLANKS' "The action that President Trump is taking is starkly un-presidential and demeaning to his office and his standing as the leader of the free world," Seneca argued. "His blatant disrespect toward the Seneca people, other Haudenosaunee nations, and all Indigenous people is unacceptable." He noted that first President George Washington signed a treaty with several nations, including the Seneca, in 1794 "promising to live in peace and friendship with one another." "The United States also promised our people the free use and enjoyment of our lands forever," Seneca said. "President Trump’s aggression toward our culture with his Executive Order violates that peace, friendship and commitments of the Canandaigua treaty." "This is the latest in a long history of willful attempts to disregard the United States’ commitments to the Seneca and other Haudenosaunee nations," he continued. "President Trump needs to be reminded of those commitments." He added that Article 6 of the U.S. Constitution "clearly states that treaties are the ‘supreme Law of the Land,’ and need to always be honored as such." HOUSE DEM'S 'LAKE NATALIE' JAB AT TRUMP AIDE SETS SOCIAL MEDIA ABLAZE: 'STAY CLASSY' Seneca called on all Native groups and federal, state and local representatives — "regardless of political party" — to stand against the name change. "We will always call Lake Ontario by the name derived from the language of our ancestors — the name that, like the strength and influence of the Seneca people, will live on forever, long after the intrusive political tirades of individual men," he said. ‘CAPTAIN CANADA’ FIREBRAND UNLOADS ON TRUMP WITH PROFANE ONE-LINER AS TRADE WAR ESCALATES Trump announced the name change on Thursday. "The Lake of America was something I've been thinking about for a long time, actually," he told reporters while signing the Executive Order in the Oval Office. "As you know, we took something called the Gulf of Mexico — we changed it — and now it's very routinely the Gulf of America," Trump said in the Oval Office." TRUMP TRADE CHIEF WARNS CANADA WALKED AWAY FROM 'THE BEST DEAL' TO TRIGGER 50% U.S. TARIFFS The president said he had directed Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and the department to update the Geographic Names Information System to reflect the name change. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney condemned the name change on X, writing, "The name is more than 400 years old, predating both the Confederation of Canada and the Declaration of Independence of the United States of America. We know that America is changing. Their trading relationships, their foreign policies, their national monuments, their hydronyms. Canadians also know that naming reality means calling it Lake Ontario — then, now and always." VANCE SAYS CANADA FRIENDLIER TO CHINA ON TRADE THAN TO US: 'INSANITY' The move to rename the lake, which sits on the U.S.-Canada border, came amid a breakdown in trade between both nations, with Trump accusing Ottawa of unfair trade practices. Trump floated renaming the lake hours before Carney's announcement of reciprocal tariffs on U.S. imports. TRUMP JUST EXPANDED HIS TARIFF PLAYBOOK WITH A POWERFUL TRADE WEAPON NO PRESIDENT HAS EVER USED The U.S. imposed new 50% tariffs on Canadian goods such as wine, furniture and dairy products, while Carney said U.S. trade demands proved Washington wanted to "destroy our major industries," including autos, steel and aluminum, FOX Business previously reported. "Canada has been ripping us off for a long time on trade," Trump said Thursday. "Very sadly, even the military, you know, we defend Canada for nothing. We don't get anything. They don't pay us to defend Canada." Trump also jokingly floated renaming the Atlantic and Pacific oceans. "So, if you think about it, we have a gulf and we have a lake," he said. "Now, all we need is an ocean. So maybe we'll have to change the name of the Atlantic and or the Pacific. Maybe we'll change them both." Trump previously used geographic names to make political statements, ordering the renaming of the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America. Trump’s executive order has been criticized by several governors, including Democrats New York Gov. Kathy Hochul and Wisconsin Gov. Tony Evers and Republican Vermont Gov. Phil Scott. "New York won’t be calling it that," Hochul wrote on X. Rep. Debbie Dingell, D-Michigan, announced that she plans to introduce House legislation that would nullify the change. "Donald Trump can sign all the executive orders he wants, but it will always be Lake Ontario," she wrote in a press release. "Canada is not our enemy. It is our neighbor, our ally, and one of Michigan’s most important economic partners. It is a friendship that no stroke of a pen can erase." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fox News Digital has reached out to the White House for comment. Fox News Digital's Louis Casiano contributed to this report.
